name: Copper Penny
lede: Copper Penny is a dusty, reddish brown named for the metal in small coins, with Wikipedia citing Crayola as its source.

sections.title: A coin-metal brown
sections.body: The nearest named colors on file are [[etruscan-red]], [[marsh-rose]], [[blast-off-bronze]] and [[antique-rose]], at 2.5, 2.7, 3.9 and 4.2 ΔE [1]. The 1955 ISCC-NBS system would class a close match as light reddish brown, 6.4 units of ΔE away, the same block it shares with [[blast-off-bronze]] [1]. A second library color, [[copper-rose]], is built on the same metal word but leans toward pink rather than brown [1]. In LCH terms Copper Penny is mid-toned and moderately chromatic: lightness 53, chroma 28, hue 30 degrees [1]. A fifth, slightly farther neighbor is [[antique-rose]], 4.2 ΔE away, redder [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings finds a close match to Copper Penny in 135, about 0.6 percent, as photographed [2]. Its fullest appearance is Gustav Klimt's *Women Friends* of 1916, at 38 percent coverage, and its heaviest use, relative to each painter's own baseline, falls to Klimt and Henri Matisse, both working in the early 1900s [2]. The color's use across the archive also skews toward Nepal and India, over 21 and 13 times the expected rate, and peaks in paintings from the 1890s [2].
